title: QProfile runtime sampling & fallback demo - DataForge
summary: Quick walkthrough of Optimize console qprofile runtime sampling, how automatic fallback works between FP8 and INT8 variants, and a short live demo of latency vs quality sampling. Customer is exploring a pilot to reduce token cost while keeping 99th percentile latency under 250ms for short prompts. Agreed next steps: run a 48h sampling job with customer's prompt set, share security checklist, follow up benchmarking run with private VPC config.

Maya Lopez: provide 10k-sample prompt set + representative latency SLA (due: 2026-07-16)

Leo Martinez: confirm whether DataForge wants private or dedicated pilot (due: 2026-07-20)

Schedule 30m bench review to inspect P99 tail causes (tentative 2026-07-21)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-14 15:00 PDT | Duration: 58 mins | Attendees: Sara Kim, Ravi Patel (Redwood); Maya Lopez, Jonah Park, Asha Gupta, Leo Martinez (DataForge)

Summary section (auto): walk through qprofile runtime sampling in Optimize, demo fallback rules between FP8/INT8, discuss latency tradeoffs and security questions.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Sara): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick check - is this still 3pm your side Maya?
00:06 Speaker 2 (Maya): Yep, all good, thanks. We have Jonah and Leo from infra on, Asha for product.
00:12 Speaker 1 (Sara): Awesome. Agenda: quick context, demo of runtime sampling and the console, show fallback rules in a sandbox, then Q&A. Ravi will run the demo.
00:25 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Hi all. Real quick context for DataForge — you mentioned you want to run assistant-style completions for short prompts and keep P99 under 250ms, right?
00:34 Speaker 2 (Maya): Exactly. Our goal is to reduce per-token spend by 30% while not degrading quality for the top-3 intents. We have some internal evals but want to see live behavior across production-ish traffic.
00:44 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Perfect. The approach we'll show: runtime sampling with qprofiles where we sample a subset of requests to FP8 to measure fidelity difference vs INT8 baseline, adaptive fallback rules that route slow or low-confidence outputs back to higher precision, and an automated canary/rollback policy.
00:56 Speaker 4 (Jonah): How many samples do you usually need to get statistical significance?
01:02 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Typically 10k to 50k samples depending on target metric. For accuracy on top intents you can get a rough signal with 10k, for edge-case fidelity you'll want 30–50k. The Optimize console will run the sampling job for you and provide quality deltas and latency histograms.
01:17 Speaker 2 (Maya): Cool. Show us the console.
01:22 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Opening the Optimize qprofile panel now. Note: the UI is an internal sandbox so some labels might be off, sorry about that.
01:30 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Here we have a job config: sample ratio 5%, seed 42, evaluation set = user-provided prompts. For this demo I've loaded a trimmed prompt set from DataForge (approx 2k).
01:44 Speaker 4 (Jonah): The seed — does that affect randomness across runs? We need reproducibility for audits.
01:49 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Yes, seed ensures reproducible sampling. We also persist the sampled IDs for later audit. We keep KV cache keys sanitized; we never store PII.
01:58 Speaker 1 (Sara): Quick security note: we'll share our security checklist and KMS options. DataForge, do you need HSM level key control?
02:05 Speaker 2 (Maya): Possibly; for a pilot we can use standard KMS but long term we may require tenant-managed keys.
02:12 Speaker 3 (Ravi): That's supported on Private deployments and Dedicated with BYOK. We'll include that in the checklist.
02:20 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Back to the demo — here's a latency histogram for the INT8 baseline. P50 ~ 40ms, P95 ~ 120ms, P99 ~ 260ms for long prompts. FP8 variant shows P50 ~ 35ms, P95 ~ 110ms, P99 ~ 320ms — so lower median but heavier tail in this model build.
02:40 Speaker 5 (Asha): Interesting, FP8 median is slightly faster but P99 worse. Why would that happen?
02:45 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Good question. FP8 can use different kernels and might change numeric stability on corner-case tokens, which can cause retries or longer KV misses. Also our runtime for FP8 maybe on a different shard layout causing slight tail effects. The console breaks out per-sequence length and shows which sequences cause degradation.
03:05 Speaker 4 (Jonah): Can the console auto-create fallback rules for sequences that exceed a latency threshold?
03:09 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Yes. You can set rules: e.g., if inference latency > 300ms or if quality delta exceeds 0.04 (on your metric), then route that request to the FP32/FP16 variant or a different shard with higher memory. The demo shows an example rule.
03:25 Speaker 5 (Asha): How does this interact with batching? Our traffic is bursty — batching helps cost but hurts tail latency.
03:28 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Optimize suggests batch sizes per route based on observed latency budget. For very latency-sensitive routes we recommend continuous batching with small micro-batches and aggressive pre-warm. The qprofile sampling includes the batch context so the quality measurement reflects the real serving regime.
03:45 Speaker 2 (Maya): We run a lot of short prompts under 32 tokens. How do int8/fp8 behave there?
03:51 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Short seqs usually favor INT8 for tail stability but FP8 can have better compression and lower cost on some kernels. That's why we do the runtime sampling — it shows per-token and per-intent deltas.
04:05 Speaker 1 (Sara): Let's run a quick sampling job with the 2k set to show the console output. Ravi, kick it off.
04:11 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Kicking off sampling now. Note: this is a shadow-run — requests are duplicated and only sample ratio hits the FP8 variant. Results will stream into the dashboard.
04:22 Speaker 3 (Ravi): While that runs, quick note on canary: you can roll out a model variant to 1% of traffic for N hours, monitor quality and latency, then auto-increment if metrics are within bounds, otherwise rollback automatically.
04:35 Speaker 4 (Jonah): If we rollback, do we incur double cost from sampled requests?
04:39 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Sampled requests add marginal cost during the sampling window but we cap the ratio. Canary cost is similar to normal traffic proportionally. We can estimate cost delta before running.
04:50 Speaker 2 (Maya): What about telemetry — do we get token-level logs and KV cache stats?
04:56 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Yes, per-request telemetry available in Console for the sample set: token breakdown, cache hits, kernel metrics, and a simplified quality diff view that shows tokens with highest divergence. Full logs can be retained in your S3 or internal log system depending on retention choices.
05:12 Speaker 4 (Leo): On private deployment, how does sampling work across VPC?
05:16 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We run the sampling logic in the private control plane or in-place if you'd like — it's flexible. For sensitive data we only persist hashed IDs and masked traces. We'll include the exact config in the security doc.
05:28 Speaker 2 (Maya): Ok seeing the sampling job progress — the dashboard shows first 500 samples.
05:33 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Yep. First quick stat: sampled FP8 quality delta for top-3 intents: mean BLEU-like metric difference 0.012 (rough), which is under your 0.02 threshold. But P99 divergence shows 6 sequences with >0.05 delta.
05:51 Speaker 5 (Asha): Can we see which sequences caused that?
05:54 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Clicking into the failure table — here's one prompt that triggers long-tail behavior, it contains an unusual tokenization pattern and rare named entities. This is where we set a fallback rule: route that prompt fingerprint to INT8 baseline.
06:12 Speaker 4 (Jonah): How deterministic is the fingerprinting? If prompt slightly changes, will it still match?
06:17 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We fingerprint on normalized prompt embeddings and some structural heuristics, thresholded to avoid false positives. It's tunable. For safety we can create a rule that triggers on N-gram overlap and sequence length too.
06:30 Speaker 2 (Maya): Pricing question — what's the cost delta if 10% of traffic hits FP8 sampling at 5% sample ratio vs full FP8 rollout?
06:38 Speaker 1 (Sara): Roughly, sampling adds ~0.5–2% cost depending on sample ratio. Full FP8 rollout reduces cost per-token by ~15–30% depending on model and quant method. We'll provide an estimate for your traffic shape after we get the 48h run.
06:55 Speaker 5 (Asha): Any known model families where FP8 consistently underperforms?
07:01 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Some LLaMA-derived models showed numeric stability issues at extreme temperatures, but many newer open models have FP8 kernels tuned. That's why we advise a sampling-first approach.
07:12 Speaker 2 (Maya): Security again — SOC2 and SSO. Do you have SOC2 Type II?
07:17 Speaker 1 (Sara): Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we have SAML SSO and RBAC. We'll share the compliance pack after the call.
07:27 Speaker 4 (Leo): For pilot isolation, would Dedicated pools be better than hosted? We need predictable P99 latency.
07:33 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and predictable throughput; we can configure burst limits and pre-warmed nodes for tail control. Private deployment offers full network isolation and BYOK. We'll include recommended options in the follow-up.
07:47 Speaker 5 (Asha): Are there telemetry quotas? We don't want to overload our observability stack.
07:50 Speaker 3 (Ravi): You can stream a sampled subset of logs out; by default we keep condensed metrics and the sampled raw logs for the sampling window only.
08:02 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Jumping back to the dashboard — the sampling stat page also shows latency vs quality binned by sequence length. For under-32 tokens the delta is acceptable; for 200+ tokens FP8 had larger divergence.
08:18 Speaker 2 (Maya): Most of our traffic is under 64 tokens so this is promising.
08:22 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Good. Also worth noting: we provide a qprofile tuning assistant that suggests quantization parameters (block sizes, per-channel scale) based on your eval set. It will propose an INT8 baseline and a FP8 variant, plus a fallback rule set.
08:36 Speaker 5 (Asha): Can that assistant be exported as a CI job? We want to incorporate into our pipeline.
08:40 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Yes, you can export the sampling pipeline as a reproducible job (YAML) and run it in your CI or our console.
08:47 Speaker 4 (Jonah): On rollouts, is there a way to throttle based on model compute capacity? If a shard gets overloaded it shouldn't automatically route more to the variant.
08:55 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We have smart-routing policies that consider node utilization and estimated token cost; you can set soft and hard caps per model variant. If a shard is near capacity, routing shifts to another variant or region.
09:09 Speaker 2 (Maya): Are there metrics for quality drift over time? We care about model degradation across weekly data shifts.
09:15 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Yes, Optimize includes ongoing regressions monitoring tied to prompt sets; you get alerts when quality delta crosses thresholds and a snapshot comparison.
09:24 Speaker 1 (Sara): Let's fast-forward — the sampling job finished for the 2k set, I'll narrate the key results while Ravi grabs the table.
09:30 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Results: FP8 vs INT8, overall quality delta 0.011, median latency 8% better on FP8, P99 latency 12% worse for FP8 on a 1% subset. We flagged 6 problematic prompt patterns and suggested fallback rules.
09:48 Speaker 5 (Asha): Ok that seems manageable. If we set fallback to route flagged patterns to INT8, what's the expected cost impact?
09:53 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Minimal — flagged patterns are <0.2% of traffic in this sample. The main cost savings still come from rolling out FP8 for safe routes.
10:02 Speaker 4 (Leo): If we want to run the 48h production sampling, what's the infra work on our side?
10:07 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We'll need a service account, sample prompt set, and networking preference (hosted vs private). For private, we need VPC peering info and KMS details. The Redwood team will provide scripts to bootstrap the sampling job.
10:20 Speaker 2 (Maya): Can we get a preview of the security doc now?
10:23 Speaker 1 (Sara): I'll email after this call. It includes SOC2, encryption-at-rest, key options, and retention policies.
10:30 Speaker 5 (Asha): A behavioral question — suppose FP8 introduces occasional hallucinations on rare intents. Does the system automatically detect weird outputs?
10:38 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We have heuristic detectors tied to reference outputs and embedding-similarity checks. A large divergence triggers a quality alert and can be part of the rollback rule. It's not a full correctness oracle, but it prevents obvious regressions.
10:54 Speaker 2 (Maya): Great. Any other concerns? Jonah?
10:57 Speaker 4 (Jonah): One more — what about model updates? If the underlying model changes, do we re-run sampling automatically?
11:02 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We can set sampling to re-run on new model releases or on a schedule. Many customers run weekly sanity sampling plus an on-deploy canary.
11:10 Speaker 1 (Sara): Wrapping up — agreed actions: Ravi will share sampling-run template; Maya will share a 10k prompt snapshot; Sara will send security + pricing; Leo to confirm deployment type. We'll run the 48h job once we get the data.
11:22 Speaker 2 (Maya): Sounds good, thanks.
11:25 Speaker 1 (Sara): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with details and a tentative review meeting next week.

Notes: occasional transcriber errors: some product names in UI were truncated, speaker label switched between Speaker 1 and Sara at times. There was one short audio glitch at ~06:00 where a sentence overlapped.

End of transcript.
